title: US yields jump after hawkish Fed signals
whatHappened: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose about 25 basis points after several Fed officials signalled that rates will stay higher for longer. Long-dated bonds and rate-sensitive assets such as REITs sold off.
whyItMatters: Portfolios holding long-duration USD bonds or REITs take the largest mark-to-market hit. Short-dated bonds are barely affected, and new money can now lock in higher yields.
clientSummary: US interest rates now look likely to stay higher for longer, and bond yields rose sharply overnight. When yields rise, the prices of long-dated bonds and of property trusts (REITs) tend to fall.
clientTalkingPoint: Higher yields also work in your favour over time: maturing bonds and new money can be reinvested at better rates than a few months ago.
stressTest: The view rests on our reading of Fed communication. Check it against the next inflation release: a soft number could reverse part of the move.

title: Big Tech funds AI capex with record bond issuance
briefHeadline: Big Tech borrowing heavily for AI
whatHappened: Large US technology companies issued a record volume of bonds in a single week to fund AI data centres. Technology credit spreads widened, tech shares slipped, and notes linked to them moved closer to their barriers.
whyItMatters: The companies remain highly rated, but heavy supply puts pressure on existing tech bonds, and investors are questioning the return on AI spending. Structured notes on tech underlyings are the most sensitive.
clientSummary: The largest US technology companies borrowed a record amount last week to pay for AI data centres. The sheer volume of new bonds pushed down the prices of existing technology bonds, and technology shares slipped as well.
clientTalkingPoint: The companies involved remain financially strong. The question the market is asking is about the pace of spending, not about their ability to repay.
stressTest: The view assumes supply stays heavy. Check it against the upcoming earnings season: strong AI revenue could quickly restore confidence.

title: New sanctions tighten oil supply
whatHappened: New sanctions on two major crude exporters were announced overnight. Brent rose about 6% as traders priced in lower supply.
whyItMatters: Energy producers benefit directly from higher prices. Airlines face higher fuel costs, which squeezes margins where hedging is limited.
clientSummary: New sanctions on two major oil exporters were announced overnight, and the oil price rose sharply. Energy companies gain from higher prices, while airlines face a larger fuel bill.
clientTalkingPoint: This is a factual market development. How long prices stay high depends on how the sanctions are enforced and on how other producers respond.

intradayUpdate.note: Update 13:10 SGT: the sanctions were widened to cover shipping and insurance. Brent extended its gain to about 10%, and the estimated moves for energy and airlines have been raised.

title: China announces new stimulus package
briefHeadline: Asian shares up on new stimulus
whatHappened: Beijing announced a package of consumer subsidies, property support and local government refinancing that was larger than the market expected. Mainland and Hong Kong equities rallied.
whyItMatters: Clients holding China or Hong Kong equities and Asian credit see gains, which opens a rebalancing conversation. Clients with little Asian exposure may ask whether they are missing out.
clientSummary: China announced a larger than expected package to support consumers and the property market. Chinese and Hong Kong shares rose strongly in response.
clientTalkingPoint: Earlier stimulus rallies faded when implementation was slow, so we would add or trim in steps instead of making one large move.
stressTest: The view assumes the measures are implemented quickly. Check it against the detail and timing of the announcements over the coming weeks.
